heard: A frozen world takes 11,000 years to orbit our sun. Most astronomers assume Neptune's gravity controlled everything out there, but dwarf planet Sedna never comes close to Neptune. At its farthest point, it swings 900 astronomical units away. Tholen hydrocarbon sludge gives its 1,000-kilometer surface a deep red glow. Hubble proved it rotates every 10 hours with no moon nearby. Neptune couldn't drag it into this extreme oval path. A passing star or an unseen planet 9 pulled it away. That left this red world on an 11,000 year journey around our Sun.
